properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The repository's central algorithm: every tool here either cracks, harvests, or spends secp256k1 keys. Classical, Shor-vulnerable; deadline risk rather than harvest risk.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Offline wallet password cracker: unauthenticated CBC is inherent to the Bitcoin Core wallet format it attacks — changeable only upstream, observable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Committed 1024-bit DSA private key (PKCS#8 `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----` blob, OID 1.2.840.10040.4.1) used as the nonce-reuse test vector in README.md and tests/test_ecdsa_key_recovery.py:91; the test at line 103 generates DSA.generate(1024) to match. Test credential, not production material; changeable here. Note the key is 1024-bit — below the 2048-bit classical bar, so the object's DSA-2048 assumption is optimistic.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RSA capability of the declared pycrypto/pycryptodomex dependencies of the ecdsa-private-key-recovery package — dependency inventory entry; the package's own code paths use DSA/ECC, not RSA, but the shipped environment provides RSA-encrypt/sign. Unmaintained pycrypto especially should be replaced.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: brainflayer hashes candidate brainwallet pubkeys with Keccak-256 to match Ethereum addresses; vendored implementation shipped in the build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES capability of the declared pycrypto/pycryptodomex dependencies (setup.py install_requires); the application's own code in this package uses DSA/ECC, AES arrives with the libraries. Dependency-inventory entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pycryptodomex is imported directly (`import Cryptodome.PublicKey.DSA`, `import Cryptodome.PublicKey.ECC`) for key conversion between pycrypto and PyCryptodome objects; version unpinned. Active, maintained fork of PyCryptodome under the Cryptodome namespace.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The pure-python `ecdsa` library implements ECDSA over secp256k1 (and NIST curves); every ECDSA operation in ecdsa-private-key-recovery, electrum-cracker and wallet-collision runs through it. Unpinned version; pure-python ECDSA is also far slower than the C libs, but that is an operational note, not a PQ one.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pycrypto (CVE-2013-7459, abandoned since 2013) is declared alongside its successor pycryptodomex and imported via the shared `Crypto` namespace — the installed one wins ambiguously. Replaceable here: drop pycrypto, keep one maintained provider.
